name: Scales Corporation Limited
overview: Scales Corporation is a New Zealand-listed diversified agribusiness group founded in 1897, operating three divisions: Global Proteins (petfood ingredients and edible protein trading and processing in the US, Australia, New Zealand and Europe), Horticulture (Mr Apple, New Zealand's largest vertically integrated apple grower/packer/exporter, plus juice manufacturer Profruit and fresh-produce exporter Fern Ridge, all Hawke's Bay-based), and Logistics (air and sea freight, mainly perishables, servicing both internal Group volumes and external customers). Since 2024 the company has pursued an aggressive step-acquisition strategy in Global Proteins, consolidating several previously part-owned joint ventures, which has made revenue and reported earnings far larger and more volatile than the underlying organic business.

business_model.summary: Scales earns money three ways: (1) trading margin on procuring, processing and marketing petfood ingredients and edible/offal proteins globally (Global Proteins - now the largest and fastest-growing segment after 2025 M&A); (2) growing, packing and exporting premium and traditional apple varieties plus juice concentrate (Horticulture/Mr Apple - the historical core, now benefiting from a multi-year shift into higher-margin Premium varieties sold into Asia/Middle East); (3) freight-forwarding/logistics margin on ocean and air freight for perishables, both intercompany and third-party (Logistics). Revenue is overwhelmingly transactional/seasonal (physical commodity and food trading, apple crop sales) rather than recurring/subscription in nature, though repeat B2B customer relationships in petfood ingredients and long-standing retail/distribution partnerships in Asia for Mr Apple provide some stickiness. Customers are B2B: international food/petfood manufacturers and distributors, fresh-produce importers, and both Group and external logistics customers.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - international food/petfood manufacturers, distributors, importers, and freight customers (both internal Group and external); no single external customer >10% of Group revenue per FY2025 10-K equivalent disclosure
business_model.geographic_mix: FY2025 revenue by market: Asia $364.7m (41%), North America $361.7m (40%), New Zealand $123.4m (14%), Europe $30.2m (3%), Other $20.0m (2%). Non-current assets located in New Zealand, Australia, the Netherlands and the USA.

main_competitors: Zespri (kiwifruit, adjacent NZ horticulture exporter, competes for orchard land/labour/logistics)
T&G Global / other NZ apple growers-exporters (Turners & Growers, Apollo, Freshmax)
Alliance Group / ANZCO / Affco (NZ meat/protein processors, some petfood by-product overlap)
US petfood-ingredient renderers and toll processors (regional independents; Darling Ingredients at larger scale)
Independent freight forwarders and 3PLs in NZ/Australia perishable logistics
competitive_position.market_position: New Zealand's largest fully vertically integrated apple grower/exporter (Mr Apple owns/leases ~17% of national apple export volume); a mid-scale but rapidly consolidating international player in petfood-ingredient sourcing/processing following the 2025 roll-up of previously-JV businesses (Meateor Australia, Fayman/ANZ Exports, Shelby step-up); a niche perishables logistics provider in NZ/Australia rather than a scale player against global 3PLs.

moat_factors.description: Owns orchards, packhouses, coolstores and brand (Mr Apple, Dazzle, Posy) end-to-end, capturing margin at each stage and enabling faster, better-quality export execution than growers who sell through third parties.

moat_factors.factor: Plant Variety Rights / Premium apple genetics
moat_factors.description: Proprietary and licensed Premium varieties (Dazzle, Posy) command materially higher FOB prices in Asia/Middle East than traditional varieties; ~79% of FY2026 export volume is forecast Premium vs 74% in FY2025, a genuine multi-year structural margin driver.

Owning (rather than JV-sharing) Meateor Australia, Fayman/ANZ Exports and Shelby gives full P&L control, supply-chain integration and cross-selling across NZ/Australia/US collection networks, but the segment still competes in a commoditised, price-taking raw-material market with tight supply.

moat_factors.factor: Brand and retail relationships in Asia
moat_factors.description: Mr Apple has invested for years in Tmall, WeChat, RedNote/Douyin presence and in-store branding across China/SE Asia, a slow-to-replicate advantage for a commodity export product.
Weather/crop risk in Horticulture is partially offset by Global Proteins and Logistics, smoothing group-level earnings versus a pure-play apple exporter.

weaknesses: No single division has a genuine structural moat - apples, meat/petfood by-products and freight are all largely price-taking, commodity-adjacent businesses
Geographic concentration of the apple crop in Hawke's Bay leaves Horticulture exposed to a single-region weather event (proven by Cyclone Gabrielle in FY2023)
Edible Proteins trading (Fayman/ANZ) is explicitly a lower-margin, higher-revenue trading business (single-digit EBITDA margin) that dilutes group margin quality even as it adds scale
Reliance on RSE (Recognised Seasonal Employer) migrant labour for orchard harvest, a policy- and pipeline-dependent input
Small-cap NZX liquidity and a market cap well under the scale of global protein/produce majors limits ability to compete for the largest M&A or supply contracts

growth_drivers: Continued shift of Mr Apple's export mix toward Premium varieties (Dazzle, Posy) and Asia/Middle East markets, structurally lifting average FOB pricing and margin (79% Premium mix targeted FY2026 vs 74% FY2025, sales to Asia/Middle East ~91% of FY2026 forecast volume vs 84% FY2025)

Global Proteins step-acquisitions of Meateor Australia, Fayman International/ANZ Exports and Shelby JV (60%->67.5%) consolidating previously-JV earnings, with a raised FY27 Underlying EBITDA target of $85m (from $70m) for the division
New fish and poultry petfood-ingredient joint venture established in the US, a low-risk/low-capital entry into adjacent protein categories
New processing facility in the Netherlands and two new in-plant collection/cooling systems in the US expanding Global Proteins processing capacity
Logistics volume growth (record airfreight, particularly dairy-sector related, plus steady sea-freight growth) leveraging both internal Group and external freight demand
Ongoing M&A pipeline - management explicitly continues to "assess further upgrade, integration and M&A opportunities" across Global Proteins and Logistics
Bostock orchard integration (acquired 2024) fast-tracking the Premium-variety redevelopment programme in Horticulture

business.risk: Reported earnings are inflated by non-repeatable acquisition-accounting gains
business.description: FY2025's $40.6m 'Other income' / 'gain on fair value of equity investment' consisted almost entirely of IFRS 3 step-acquisition remeasurement gains recognised when previously-held 50% equity interests in FIG/Fayman (~$23.9m) and ANZ Exports (~$2.5m) were revalued to fair value on obtaining control - a one-off, non-cash accounting gain, not operating cash flow. Reported NPATAS of $101.0m in FY2025 should not be extrapolated; Underlying NPATAS of $61.8m is the more representative (though still M&A-boosted) measure.

business.risk: European JV partner collapse forced consolidation of a loss-making, negative-net-asset business
business.description: Esro Food Group B.V. (Scales' 50% JV partner in Esro Petfood, following a Dutch food-safety authority investigation and subsequent receivership/bankruptcy of the partner) triggered Scales gaining accounting control of Esro Petfood on 23 June 2026. Esro Petfood had negative net assets of -$20.3m at the change-of-control date and Scales booked a $19.9-20.2m impairment on its related-party loan to the JV in H1-2026. Esro's underlying loss was $5.8m in H1-2026 alone (Group share $2.9m) and management describes the situation as an ongoing 'disruption' requiring stabilisation.

business.risk: Hawke's Bay geographic and weather concentration in apples
business.description: Cyclone Gabrielle (Feb 2023) caused a $13.2m goodwill/asset write-down at Mr Apple and drove NPATAS down to just $5.2m in FY2023 (from $19.4m FY2022) - proof the core Horticulture earnings stream can be severely and abruptly impaired by a single weather event given the orchard concentration in one region.

business.risk: Customer and market concentration / edible proteins is a low-margin trading business
business.description: Global Proteins' 'Edible Proteins' trading units (Fayman/ANZ Exports) operate at high revenue but single-digit EBITDA margins (~9% blended in H1-2026 vs ~24% a year earlier before consolidation), and consolidation of this trading revenue has structurally diluted the division's reported margin percentage even while absolute EBITDA dollars grow.
Mr Apple relies on >1,000 Recognised Seasonal Employer workers at peak; policy changes or labour shortages would directly constrain harvest and pack-out.

business.risk: Integration risk from a rapid, multi-deal M&A programme
business.description: FY2025 alone consolidated four previously-JV or minority-owned businesses (Meateor Australia, Fayman/ANZ Exports, Shelby step-up) across three countries; goodwill has grown from $40.6m to $168.8m (and $172.9m at H1-2026) in one year, raising execution and impairment risk if any of these businesses underperform.

financial.risk: Rising debt funding the acquisition spree
financial.description: Net debt moved from net cash of $12.5m (FY2024) to net debt of $84.1m (FY2025) to $106.7m (H1-2026, seasonally elevated), funding ~AUD 91m of Australian acquisitions plus USD 24.4m for the Shelby step-up. Total borrowings plus IFRS-16 lease liabilities were roughly $274m at H1-2026. Leverage remains moderate (0.7x net debt/EBITDA, 18.5% net debt/equity) and term facilities were extended to July 2029 in August 2026, but the trajectory is upward.

Mr Apple's FY2025 currency exposure was 79% USD, 7% EUR, 5% GBP, 5% JPY, 4% CAD; Global Proteins and Logistics also carry USD/AUD/EUR exposure. Hedging (up to 5 years forward for Mr Apple) mitigates but does not eliminate translation and transaction risk, and a stronger NZD would compress margins.

The FIG/ANZ/Meateor Australia acquisitions include AUD ~36.4m (NZD ~41.5m) of deferred consideration payable in five annual instalments to FY2030, a fixed near-term cash outflow layered on top of ordinary capex and dividends.

Net working capital is highly seasonal (Horticulture receivables/inventory peak mid-year) and grew materially with the Edible Proteins consolidation, driving H1-2026 net debt up; management expects it to unwind in 2H26.

regulatory.description: The Esro Food Group situation originated from a Dutch food-safety authority (NVWA) investigation into the JV partner, illustrating direct regulatory risk to Global Proteins' European operations; apple export market access into China, the Middle East and other markets is also subject to phytosanitary and biosecurity requirements that can change without notice.

Scales currently prepares standalone Climate Statements; a legislative change may limit mandatory reporting to companies with market cap above $1bn, which would reduce (not increase) compliance burden, but the regime remains in flux.
Government settings on seasonal worker visa numbers and conditions directly affect Mr Apple's harvest capacity.

macro.risk: Geopolitical disruption to trade lanes and Middle East demand
macro.description: Management has repeatedly flagged 'ongoing geopolitical tension' (Middle East conflict) as impacting market access, fuel costs and freight costs across Horticulture and Logistics through FY2026, and as a specific risk to final apple pricing with ~7% of the FY2026 export crop still to be sold as at the August 2026 result.

Logistics' thin ~7-8% EBITDA margins are directly exposed to fuel price swings and global shipping disruption; sea-freight margins have already been pressured, partly offset by strong airfreight growth (dairy-sector driven).
Petfood Ingredients input costs are affected by 'lower global livestock numbers' per H1-2026 commentary, tightening supply and raising working-capital needs even as it can support pricing.
Group now carries meaningfully more term and seasonal debt than in the net-cash era pre-2025; ~42% of US dollar term debt was interest-rate-swap hedged at FY2025.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global demand for premium fresh produce (into Asia/Middle East) and for petfood ingredients (a structurally growing, less cyclical end-market than human food) both support multi-year volume and pricing tailwinds; NZ apple export volumes are recovering from the FY2023 cyclone-depressed base, and NZ's total apple crop grew 21% in FY2025.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high and multi-layered: Horticulture is weather/season-cyclical (proven by the FY2023 Cyclone Gabrielle shock and the 2019-2021 COVID shipping/labour disruption); Global Proteins is tied to global livestock supply cycles and pet ownership trends (historically defensive); Logistics tracks trade volumes and fuel costs. The blended group is less volatile than Horticulture alone but still exhibits large earnings swings (NPATAS ranged from $5.2m in FY2023 to $101.0m reported / $61.8m underlying in FY2025).
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate and rising - net debt has grown from net cash to ~$85-107m through 2025-26 to fund acquisitions; partially hedged via interest rate swaps (42% of US debt at FY2025).
key_input_costs: Raw meat/animal by-product feedstock for petfood ingredients
FX-driven input costs on offshore acquisitions/debt

recent_developments.event: Completed AUD 91.05m step-acquisitions of the remaining 50% of FI Group Holding (Fayman International/ANZ trading), a further 42.5% of ANZ Exports (to 85%) and the remaining 50% of Meateor Australia (to 100%), consolidating all three as subsidiaries; recognised ~$129m of new goodwill and ~$31.6m of non-cash step-acquisition remeasurement gains.
Increased Shelby JV LLC (US petfood cold storage/processing) shareholding from 60% to 67.5% for USD 24.4m, cancelling the associated put option over 5% of the JV.

FY2025 annual result: revenue $899.9m (+54%), Underlying EBITDA $137.6m (+50%), Underlying NPATAS $61.8m (+82%), reported NPATAS $101.0m (+233%, inflated by one-off acquisition gains); net debt swung to $84.1m from net cash $12.5m; initial FY2026 Underlying NPATAS guidance set at $50.0-55.0m.

Scales issued a market reassurance statement after Dutch authorities (NVWA) launched an investigation into Esro Food Group (Esro Petfood's 50% JV partner), stating Esro Pet Food was legally/operationally separate and undisrupted at that time.

May 2026 market update reiterated FY2026 Underlying NPATAS guidance of $50.0-55.0m; disclosed Esro Food Group subsidiary Esro Vlees BV had been placed into receivership following the NVWA investigation, disrupting the Esro Petfood JV; Mr Apple gross pick of 4.7m TCEs came in above expectations but forecast pack-out rate of 77% was below FY2025's 80% due to weather events during the growing season.

Esro Food Group B.V. filed for bankruptcy, suspending its shareholder rights and giving Scales accounting control of the previously 50/50 Esro Petfood JV; Scales impaired ~$19.9-20.2m of its related-party loan to Esro Petfood and consolidated a business with negative net assets of -$20.3m.

H1-2026 result: revenue $762.1m (+105% YoY, mostly acquisition-driven), Underlying EBITDA $102.2m (+18%), Underlying NPATAS $52.0m (+7%), reported NPATAS only $30.1m (-38% YoY) after the $19.9m Esro loan impairment; net debt rose seasonally to $106.7m; FY2026 Underlying NPATAS guidance raised to $55.0-60.0m.

guidance.as_of: H1-2026 Interim Results / Media Release (26 August 2026)

items.notes: Raised from the $50.0-55.0m range set at the FY2025 annual result (Feb 2026) and reiterated in the May 2026 market update. Implied by the FY2026 crop being sold at a faster run-rate (66% sold at 30 June 2026 vs 54% a year earlier) and stronger Global Proteins volumes.
Directors' stated implication of the NPATAS guidance range.
Directors' stated implication of the NPATAS guidance range; compares to FY2025 actual Underlying EBITDA of $137.6m, i.e. broadly flat-to-modestly-up at the midpoint despite the Esro disruption.
Increased from a prior $70m target following the consolidation of Meateor Australia, Fayman International and ANZ Exports; a medium-term divisional goal, not single-year guidance.

items.vs_prior: lowered slightly vs FY2025 actual (3.68m TCEs)
items.notes: Offset by faster sales run-rate, higher Premium mix (~79% of volume vs 74% FY2025) and stronger Asia/Middle East skew (~91% of fruit sold vs 84% FY2025); ~7% of export crop remained unsold as at the August 2026 result (vs ~18% unsold at the same point in 2025).
Group ROCE was 14.6% in FY2025, above the 12.5% long-run target; divisional ROCE targets vary by asset/risk profile.

items.target: 50%-75% of Underlying NPAT Attributable to Shareholders, split ~evenly interim/final
items.notes: FY2025 interim dividend of 12.5 cps (partially imputed) was paid Jan 2026; final 2025 dividend was also 12.5 cps, paid 9 July 2026 (with a Dividend Reinvestment Plan drawing $5.0m of reinvestment). FY2024 total dividends were 15.0 cps.

guidance.management_commentary: Chair Mike Petersen: 'The Group has delivered another record first-half result, with each of the divisional teams progressing their respective growth objectives whilst continuing to navigate ongoing geopolitical turbulence.' Management flagged three specific FY2026 second-half risk factors: (1) Mr Apple has only ~7% of the export crop left to sell, with ongoing Middle East geopolitical tension and final pricing as risks; (2) Global Proteins remains 'cautious...due to the current geopolitical environment and tight supply in certain markets' albeit 'confident with the medium-term outlook'; (3) Logistics remains 'watchful of the ongoing impact of [freight] disruption in the second half of the year.' On Esro specifically, MD Andy Borland stated the 'recent disruption at Esro Petfoods in Europe has been challenging, however our immediate focus is to stabilise operations and assess the long-term strategic plan within the region.'

bull_case: Underlying (ex one-off) earnings are genuinely compounding: 1H22-1H26 CAGRs of 25% revenue, 17% Underlying EBITDA, 19% Underlying NPATAS/EPS, driven by both organic margin mix improvement in Horticulture and successful bolt-on consolidation in Global Proteins

The Premium apple variety transition (Dazzle/Posy into Asia and the Middle East) is a multi-year, largely de-risked structural margin driver already visible in the numbers (Premium mix up from 74% to a targeted 79% of FY2026 volume) and not dependent on further M&A
Global Proteins' FY27 EBITDA target was raised to $85m (from $70m) after 2025's consolidation, giving a clear, quantified medium-term growth path management has already begun to deliver against

Conservative balance sheet by history and even after the acquisition spree - net debt/EBITDA of only ~0.7x, term facilities refinanced to 2029, and management explicitly describes its approach to capital structure as 'conservative'

Consistent, well-covered dividend policy (50-75% of Underlying NPATAS) with a demonstrated 15% compounded annual shareholder return since the 2014 IPO, well ahead of the S&P/NZX50's ~9%, plus a Dividend Reinvestment Plan providing capital-light funding flexibility
bear_case: FY2025's headline reported earnings (NPATAS $101.0m, EPS 70.7c) are not repeatable and materially overstate underlying earnings power - roughly $26m-plus of the reported NPAT was a one-off, non-cash IFRS 3 gain from remeasuring previously-held JV stakes to fair value on step-acquisition; even Underlying NPATAS of $61.8m benefited from a full or near-full year of consolidated Fayman/ANZ/Meateor Australia earnings that were only partly owned in the comparative period, so the true run-rate 'organic' earnings base is smaller than either headline suggests

The Esro Petfood situation shows the acquisition-led growth strategy carries real, crystallising downside: a JV partner's bankruptcy forced Scales to consolidate a business with negative net assets and book a ~$20m loan impairment in H1-2026 alone, and management still describes the European operations as needing to be 'stabilised' with the long-term strategic plan unresolved

Horticulture earnings power has proven fragile to a single weather event - Cyclone Gabrielle cut FY2023 NPATAS to just $5.2m (from $19.4m) with a $13.2m impairment, and Hawke's Bay orchard concentration means this risk has not been diversified away, only diluted by the now much larger (and separately risky) Global Proteins segment

Rapid, serial M&A (four consolidations in 2025 alone, goodwill quadrupling from $40.6m to $168.8m in a single year) raises integration and impairment risk, while net debt has swung from net cash ($12.5m) to over $100m in eighteen months, funding deferred-consideration obligations running to FY2030

Edible Proteins trading growth is diluting group margin quality (Global Proteins EBITDA margin fell from ~24% to ~9% as the low-margin, high-revenue Fayman/ANZ trading business was consolidated), meaning the headline 105% H1-2026 revenue growth significantly overstates the improvement in underlying profitability, and NPATAS growth of only 6.7% in the same half is the more honest read-through
